p: At approximately 3:00 PM, 12,500 Confederate soldiers stepped from the tree line on Seminary Ridge and began the mile-wide advance. Pickett's division, Pettigrew's division, and Trimble's two brigades crossed the open ground under devastating artillery and musket fire.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 14, “Pickett's Charge” (The Mile-Wide Advance), paragraph 2 of 3

p: The charge reached The Angle but was repulsed at enormous cost. Confederate casualties were approximately 50% — over 6,000 men killed, wounded, or captured. Lee rode among the survivors saying "It is all my fault." The charge marked the beginning of the end of Confederate offensive capacity.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 14, “Pickett's Charge” (The Mile-Wide Advance), paragraph 3 of 3

p: A small copse of trees on Cemetery Ridge served as the visual aiming point for Pickett's Charge and has since become known as the High Water Mark of the Confederacy — the point of maximum Confederate penetration into the Union line.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 15, “The High Water Mark” (The Copse of Trees), paragraph 1 of 3

p: The monument at the High Water Mark was dedicated in 1892. The Battlefield Memorial Association, which later became part of the NPS, was established partly to preserve this ground.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 15, “The High Water Mark” (The Copse of Trees), paragraph 2 of 3

p: General Lewis Armistead, who died after being wounded at the guns, is remembered by a marker near the copse of trees. His friendship with Union General Winfield Hancock — wounded the same afternoon — became one of the war's most poignant symbols of a nation divided against itself.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 15, “The High Water Mark” (The Copse of Trees), paragraph 3 of 3

p: On the night of July 4-5, 1863, the Army of Northern Virginia began its retreat toward Virginia. A wagon train of wounded men, 17 miles long, moved through driving rain toward the Potomac crossing at Williamsport.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 16, “Confederate Avenue” (The Retreat), paragraph 1 of 3

p: Meade chose not to pursue aggressively. President Lincoln was devastated by the failure to destroy Lee's army before it could cross the Potomac. "We had them within our grasp," Lincoln wrote. "We had only to stretch forth our hands and they were ours."

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 16, “Confederate Avenue” (The Retreat), paragraph 2 of 3

p: Lee's army crossed the swollen Potomac on July 14, escaping to Virginia. The Gettysburg campaign was over. Confederate casualties totaled approximately 28,000; Union casualties approximately 23,000. The battle proved to be the turning point of the war in the East.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 16, “Confederate Avenue” (The Retreat), paragraph 3 of 3

p: As the morning of July 1 progressed, Confederate forces under Rodes arrived on Oak Ridge north of the town, threatening the Union right flank. The XI Corps under Howard deployed north of Gettysburg to meet this threat.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 2, “Oak Ridge” (The Union Right Flank), paragraph 1 of 3

p: Iverson's North Carolina brigade advanced without skirmishers into a deadly ambush. Paul's Union brigade, concealed behind a stone wall, delivered a devastating volley. Nearly 500 Confederates surrendered in the wheat field — the largest single mass surrender of the battle.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 2, “Oak Ridge” (The Union Right Flank), paragraph 2 of 3

p: Daniel's brigade and Ramseur's brigade pressed the Union line relentlessly. By early afternoon the Union position north of town was becoming untenable.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 2, “Oak Ridge” (The Union Right Flank), paragraph 3 of 3

p: Brigadier General Francis Barlow advanced his division of the XI Corps to a slight rise north of Gettysburg — soon to bear his name. The move exposed both flanks and invited envelopment.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 3, “Barlow's Knoll” (XI Corps Exposed), paragraph 1 of 3

p: Early's division, arriving from the northeast on the Harrisburg Road, struck the exposed position from three sides simultaneously. Gordon's Georgia brigade swept forward with devastating effect.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 3, “Barlow's Knoll” (XI Corps Exposed), paragraph 2 of 3

p: Barlow was shot from his horse and left for dead on the field. Confederate General Gordon, finding him wounded, stopped to give him water and had him moved to safety. The two men would become friends after the war, debating for decades whether this encounter actually occurred.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 3, “Barlow's Knoll” (XI Corps Exposed), paragraph 3 of 3

p: By mid-afternoon on July 1, the Union position north and west of Gettysburg had become untenable. The XI Corps was streaming back through the town in disorder, and the I Corps' right flank was exposed.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (map walkthrough)
p.short: Site walkthrough stop 4, “Seminary Ridge” (The Union Retreat), paragraph 1 of 3

p: The survivors rallied on Cemetery Hill south of town, where Howard had wisely positioned a reserve. The high ground — Cemetery Hill, Culp's Hill, and the long spine of Cemetery Ridge — would become the Union fishhook line that determined the battle's outcome.

p.short: Site walkthrough stop 4, “Seminary Ridge” (The Union Retreat), paragraph 2 of 3
